newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Waikato eye Auckland's weaknesses.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Waikato eye Auckland's weaknesses.

text.p: Waikato will target specific, perceived weaknesses in the Auckland rugby team in a bid to hang on to the Ranfurly Shield in Hamilton on Friday night.
The New Zealand Press Association reported that Waikato coach John Boe has come up with a game plan to attack one or two areas where he believed Auckland may be weaker in than others.

He was not giving any details away, but he knows it will take a herculean effort for his team to compete on a level footing with an Auckland side that not only contains nine current All Blacks, including six of the test pack, but also 14 players who have played international rugby.

"We have to play better than we played against North Harbour because Auckland are a much better team than Harbour, but I think we can go up a notch in all sorts of aspects -- particularly our backplay," Boe said.
"You never know until the whistle goes, but the feeling in the team's good and the build-up has been as good if not better than for the Harbour game," he said.
There is no doubt the greatest pressure will go on Boe's forwards, who have performed so well to date.
Lock Mark Cooksley must repeat his sensational lineout play of the North Harbour game and to do that hooker Greg Smith's throws will have to be on the button.
The single biggest question can only be answered by the Waikato scrum. Can a front row averaging under 23 years of age and 18 caps compete with Auckland's world-beating All Blacks front three?
"They've got nothing to lose and everything to gain," Boe said of the young front row of Michael Collins, Greg Smith and Murray Driver.
Auckland will look to attack in this area, trying to nullify the effectiveness of bruising Waikato No 8 Deon Muir and champion openside flanker Duane Monkley.
Auckland are doing their best to undo the work of both oddsmakers and ad-makers going into the game.
Auckland team manager Rex Davy said his side were under no illusions about how tough it would be to win the shield.
"People are painting us as the favourites, but I don't think that is necessarily so. I cannot imagine a harder place to challenge for the shield than at Rugby Park," Davy said.
This is Auckland's first Ranfurly Shield challenge against Waikato in 44 years. They were unsuccessful in 1951, won it in 1952 but lost it back to Waikato two weeks later.
Auckland have had 30 shield challenges in their history and won 12 of them.
Teams:-

Waikato: Bruce Reihana, Aisea Tuilevu, Matthew Cooper, Wayne Warlow, Scott McLeod, Ian Foster, Simon Crabb, Deon Muir, Duane Monkley, Mark Cooksley, Steve Gordon (captain), Scott Miller, Murray Driver, Greg Smith, Michael Collins.
Reserves: Damien Karauna, Tommy Hayes, Rhys Duggan, Nick Holten, Tiwini Hemi, David Briggs, Richard Kirke.

Auckland: Adrian Cashmore, James Kerr, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Andrew Blowers, Richard Fromont, Robin Brooke, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick, Craig Dowd.
Reserves: Waisake Sotutu, Romi Ropati, Craig McGrath, Dylan Mika, Lio Lafaiali'i, Kevin Nepia, John Akurangi.
Referee: Colin Hawke (South Canterbury).
